### Description of the bug:


If you are using `build --nobuild_python_zip` to avoid producing the python zipfiles on windows, instead you now need to use `build --@rules_python//python/config_settings:build_python_zip=false`.

There is no warning that it is ignored and no documentation on the change. 

### Which category does this issue belong to?

_No response_

### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.


With any project that uses python executables on Windows. 
You can have can run on windows with `build --@rules_python//python/config_settings:build_python_zip=false` and you can see no zip file is created, however when you do this with `build --nobuild_python_zip` zip files are produced.

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


windows

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


release 9.0.0rc6

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.


_No response_

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin; git rev-parse HEAD` ?


```text

```

### If this is a regression, please try to identify the Bazel commit where the bug was introduced with bazelisk --bisect.


_No response_

### Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

_No response_

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

_No response_

comments.body:
`--build_python_zip=false` should work. Does that not?  

> There is no warning that it is ignored 

Will take a look. I suspect `--nobuild_python_zip` is parsing the now unused native flag, then dropping it since the native flag has no effect. Good point the silent behavior is unhelpful.
Also, we think https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/26854 will surface a warning for this sort of thing. Not sure if that'll be backported to 9.x though.

Note https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/26854 is still open. We're merging it but this that'll take a number of days as we clean up various references. 

Do we consider that a sufficient fix?

Do you mean `--build_python_zip` will work and `--nobuild_python_zip` will print a deprecated warning? I think the warning should be clear why this is happening and what the alternative is, like `--build_python_zip=false`?
@iancha1992 This is another one we should fix with 9.0.1

> Do you mean `--build_python_zip` will work and `--nobuild_python_zip` will print a deprecated warning? I think the warning should be clear why this is happening and what the alternative is, like `--build_python_zip=false`?

That's fair. We'll have to do more custom code to support that, perhaps after this week's summit.
@gregestren @dabanki Can you please take a look at this one soonish since it's a release blocker for 9.0.1, thanks!
Yes, we'll sync on this in just a bit today and follow up.
We're planning to follow up on this specific flag immediately, then soon after write code to generalize the warning to *all* boolean flags with this issue.

A fix for this issue has been included in [Bazel 9.0.1 RC1](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/releases/tag/9.0.1rc1). Please test out the release candidate and report any issues as soon as possible.
If you're using Bazelisk, you can point to the latest RC by setting USE_BAZEL_VERSION=9.0.1rc1. Thanks!
